result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B is better. Its headlines are more concrete and stick closer to the fact sheet, though the subheads repeat the same feature list. A includes unsupported claims like "More Profit," "Less Driving" and "Never Miss a Slot." It also relies on generic wording such as "Optimized" and "Smart routing," and several headlines are vague. B has small stretches too ("zero dead zones," "works everywhere"), but most of its headlines tell a van groomer what the product does. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Every claim in A comes from the fact sheet. Its weakness is that the subheads are nearly the same feature list each time; only 'Works everywhere' and 'zero dead zones' stretch the no-signal fact a little. B's headlines cover more angles, but it adds claims that aren't in the facts ('More Appointments', 'More Profit', 'Never Miss a Slot', 'Happier Clients'). It also uses filler like 'Optimize' and 'Smart routing', and several of its headlines don't tell a van groomer what the product does.
